title: Luonnontieteellisen museon Elämän historia -sali sulkeutuu vuodenvaihteen jälkeen – uusi näyttely avautuu loppuvuodesta 2028
content:
The Natural History Museum’s History of Life is one of the museum’s most popular exhibitions. However, the exhibition, completed in 2008, has long been in need of an update, as it is outdated both in terms of content and exhibition technology.

– The new exhibition will present evolution and the development of biodiversity in a more spectacular and tangible way than before. This is the museum’s most significant renewal project in years, says Sanna Vuori, Head of the Public Engagement Unit at the Finnish Museum of Natural History.

The dinosaurs Giganotosaurus carolinii and Shunosaurus lii in the History of Life exhibition have become familiar to many museum visitors over the years. They will remain in the new exhibition but will be joined by never-before-seen reconstructions of prehistoric animals. Among other things, a reconstruction of the otter-like early whale Ambulocetus natans is currently being built in the museum’s conservation facilities.

title: Southnord Artfest 2026: Roots En Route
content:
Roots En Route is a multi-sensory installation by four artists who will create a multi-sensory installation in dialogue with the greenhouses – examining rootedness and displacement; asking what grows where it was planted and what survives the crossing. The African plants that fill the greenhouses carry their own histories of movement and adaptation.

Camille Norment in collaboration with Sofia Jernberg create a soundscape drawing on the insects and birds of the plants' homelands. Toubab Holmes' site-specific scent installation traces the hidden journeys of plants through the extractive system of perfumery. Charmaine Watkiss visits the botanical legacies and healing traditions of her Caribbean ancestry through large-scale drawings of Plant Warriors. Together, the three works read the botanical garden as an archive of movement, and the plants in it as things that were carried, taken and made to travel.

Running from October 2026 through January 2027, the exhibition offers a long, unhurried encounter between art and the plant world. Set aside more time than you think you need. Walk slowly, sense carefully, and let yourself be immersed.

title: “Ilman pölyttäjiä maailma olisi ankea ja väritön” – Uusi näyttely avaa oven pölyttäjien kiehtovaan elämään
content:
Pollinators represent an astonishingly diverse group of animals, many of which possess remarkable abilities despite their small size. Bees can count, bumblebees solve problems, and on distant islands, even lizards can pollinate flowers.

The  exhibition, which combines science and art, offers a wealth of information, stunning visuals, and fun activities for visitors of all ages. Guests can play interactive games like "Identify the Pollinators" and "Pollinator Protection Bingo," design their own imaginary pollinator, and explore the museum's impressive collection of specimens. The exhibition is based on a newly illustrated non-fiction book.

– We want to show the world through the eyes of pollinators, says exhibition scriptwriter Mia Rönkä, Adjunct Professor in Environmental Ecology at the University of Turku. Rönkä has written the exhibition’s informational texts and poems.

Although the sensory perceptions, cognitive abilities, and communication methods of pollinators like bees differ from ours as humans, we can still strive to understand and appreciate them as individuals of other species – without anthropomorphizing them, Rönkä explains.

title: Ukrainan sota - yliopiston suositukset
content:
The University of Helsinki has condemned the military action by Russia and expressed its support for Ukraine and its university community. We have also expressed our support for Ukraine, together with other Finnish universities, through statements by and the . As a demonstration of support, we have illuminated buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag and raised the flag on our premises.

One of the principles of the University of Helsinki is to promote international collaboration in research and higher education, and to support these efforts even in difficult circumstances. Russia’s indefensible military aggression in Ukraine has required exceptional measures, which include those taken in the collaboration between universities.

The University of Helsinki is monitoring both national and EU-level sanctions, adapting our policies and processes accordingly. Together with other Finnish and international universities, the University of Helsinki strives to promote the end of military action in Ukraine, while supporting Ukrainian institutions and people.

title: Linguistic and cultural sustainability: Perspectives across Languages and Cultures
content:
We invite contributions examining how languages and cultures interact with their social, political, ideological, educational, and ecological environments, and how these interactions shape sustainable linguistic and cultural practices. The workshop thus aims to bring different disciplinary and methodological perspectives together. We welcome contributions that develop conceptual, methodological, empirical, or practice-based approaches to linguistic and cultural sustainability. Given the research profile of CoCoLaC, we particularly welcome contributions focusing on Germanic and Romance languages and cultures. Contributions addressing other languages, cultures, and comparative contexts are equally welcome. 

You can find the call for papers .

title: HIKET at UN climate change conference COP31
content:
12 November 2026, 18.30–20.00
Side Event Room Brown, Blue Zone, COP31, Antalya

The reliability of land-use sector climate data is crucial for implementing the Paris Agreement, as around 25% of the mitigation planned in countries' Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) relies on the land sector. At our event, "The importance of an integrated framework for AFOLU carbon balance", we will explore how greenhouse gas inventories, ground-based and atmospheric observations and satellite data together can support the reconciliation of land-sector carbon balance and their uncertainty estimates. This is essential for accelerating public and private climate actions.

As tropical deforestation and #peatland emissions are among the sector's biggest global climate challenges, we will consider with our partners how this integrated framework approach could be co-developed and scaled from boreal to tropics.

The event is co-hosted with ICOS - Integrated Carbon Observation System, Landscape Alliance | CIFOR & ICRAF and the Ministry of Forestry of the Republic of Indonesia.

14 November 2026, 10.00–10.45
Finland Pavilion, Blue Zone, COP31, Antalya

title: Small changes can have a big impact on sustainability transitions
content:
In her dissertation, examines how public policies, such as policy strategies and legislation, influence transitions towards the circular economy and sustainability. Entsalo works as a researcher in the Circular Economy Solutions Unit at the Finnish Environment Institute. Her work focuses on circular economy policy instruments, sustainability transitions, and innovation policy, particularly at the national and EU levels.

The circular economy means a system change that aims to reduce the use of raw materials and generation of waste by, for example, designing products that are more durable and repairable. Circular economy policies have often sought to reconcile economic and environmental objectives. However, sustainability goals can easily be overshadowed by more immediate concerns and economic priorities, making public policies essential for advancing sustainability.

“Public policies can drive significant societal reforms, but they can also shift responsibility elsewhere and dilute previously established goals,” Entsalo says.

title: Two WEIRD-inspired master’s theses completed and available
content:
Sasha’s thesis, situated within the field of social psychology, focuses on how queer migrant environmental activists discursively construct environmental activism through an analysis of audio podcasts. The study combines intersectional and critical discursive psychology approaches to understand how marginalized identities, shaped by power relations and structural inequalities, at the same time function as discursive resources.  

The findings show that queer migrant environmental activists seek discursive authority, allowing them to construct activism through careful navigation of contradictions between the “transformational” and “neoliberal” image of environmental action; between the constructed “transformative” ideals and relatively pragmatic and institutionalized activist practices; between belonging to the activist community and exclusion from it; and between collective identity and intersectional positioning. Environmental activism is mainly presented as “Societal Transformation,” representing activist ideals, and “Collective Belonging,” reflecting contested belonging and collective identity negotiations.

title: Lahjoita: Tekoäly ansaitsee opetuksen
content:
“It’s important that pupils and students learn to actively use AI for learning, while also learning to study with it and use it adaptably in their studies on their own and with others.”

“This is why banning AI use in schools is a non-starter. On the contrary, pupils and students must be made to use it more appropriately,” Toom emphasises. For the time being, the situation is different: it can depend on the municipality, educational institution and even the teacher whether children and adolescents use AI in learning.

The problem is precisely that today’s schools do not necessarily teach them AI skills with sufficient goal orientation.

This is why our goal is to establish Finland’s first professorship in pedagogical AI. The position would strengthen research on AI in teaching and learning, as well as generate knowledge on what future teachers must know about AI. 

In addition to the professorship, the funds raised will be spent on national continuing education for teachers already serving in their profession. They will be taught the most important aspects of AI in education, teaching and learning.

content: Members of the Conservation and Sustainability Research Group brought together their broad range of expertise in conservation to write a perspective piece on conservation data gaps and their implications for the Global Biodiversity Framework (GBF) targets.
